title: Nadella Addresses Indian American Tech CEOs at Seattle's Ideas4India Forum
excerpt: More than 40 Indian-origin CEOs and CTOs gathered at the Consulate General of India in Seattle for a forum on deepening India-US technology cooperation.
body:
• Microsoft chairman and CEO Satya Nadella was the guest of honour at "Ideas4India: Indian American Tech CEOs Forum | Unlocking the Tech Dividend," hosted by the Consulate General of India in Seattle on September 17.
  • More than 40 Indian-origin CEOs and CTOs from the Greater Seattle and Pacific Northwest technology ecosystem took part, in an event framed as a follow-up to the India AI Impact Summit 2026.
  • Discussions focused on deepening India-US technology cooperation across AI infrastructure, data centres, semiconductors, quantum research, talent and skilling, aerospace and advanced manufacturing.
  • Indian Ambassador to the US Vinay Kwatra also addressed the gathering, welcoming the participants' interest in strengthening the bilateral technology partnership.

SEATTLE — Microsoft chairman and CEO Satya Nadella addressed a gathering of more than 40 Indian-origin technology chief executives in Seattle this week, urging the region's Indian American tech community to deepen its role in the growing technology partnership between India and the United States.

The forum, titled "Ideas4India: Indian American Tech CEOs Forum | Unlocking the Tech Dividend," was hosted on September 17 by the Consulate General of India in Seattle as a follow-up to the India AI Impact Summit 2026. According to a press release from the consulate, discussions centred on strengthening technology cooperation between the two countries.

Nadella, who attended as guest of honour, spoke about the growth of Seattle's technology community over the past 35 years and its evolving relationship with India. He described the Indian American community in the Seattle region as one that wears its success lightly — "It has a culture where you do more and talk less," he said, in remarks reported by the South Asian Herald.

A bridge between two tech ecosystems

The forum drew leading Indian-origin technology executives, several of whom have spent more than three decades working at the forefront of artificial intelligence, quantum computing, semiconductors, cloud infrastructure, aerospace and enterprise software, according to the South Asian Herald's account of the event.

Participating leaders represented companies and organisations including Microsoft, Amazon, Boeing, OpenAI, Anthropic, Intel, Veeam Software, Helion, Zenoti and Viome Life Sciences, the consulate said. India’s Ambassador to the United States, Vinay Kwatra, and the Consul General of India in Seattle, Prakash Gupta, were also present.

Nadella highlighted the emergence of a technology community that contributes to economic progress, helps distribute the benefits of technology more widely, and builds stronger relationships with India. "I think it is something that I definitely am very proud of having seen, even in the last 35 years, grow from strength to strength," he said, adding that many technology leaders had played an instrumental role in that progress.

"It has a culture where you do more and talk less."

— Satya Nadella, Microsoft chairman and CEO, on Seattle's Indian American technology community

AI, semiconductors and talent on the agenda

The interactive forum provided a platform for Indian-origin technology leaders to share ideas on expanding the India-US technology partnership. According to the consulate's press release, reported by ANI, discussions covered AI infrastructure, data centres, semiconductor design and manufacturing, quantum research, talent and skilling, aerospace and advanced manufacturing.

Nadella described artificial intelligence as a general-purpose technology and said its benefits would depend on broad diffusion across countries, communities and sectors — a framing that positions India's large talent pool and the diaspora's technical leadership as central to how AI spreads globally.

The timing matters. The forum follows the India AI Impact Summit 2026, where New Delhi has been pressing its case as a destination for AI infrastructure investment, and it comes as Washington and New Delhi continue negotiating the terms of technology cooperation on semiconductors, critical minerals and emerging technologies.

Why Seattle, why now

Seattle's claim on the diaspora story is specific. The city is home to one of the densest concentrations of Indian-origin technology executives in the world, spread across Microsoft, Amazon, a wave of cloud startups and deep-tech ventures. Nadella himself has led Microsoft since 2014, and his tenure has made him the most visible symbol of that community's ascent.

For India, the forum is part of a broader diplomatic push to convert diaspora networks into technology partnerships. Kwatra's presence alongside the consulate's hosting signals that New Delhi treats the Indian American tech leadership as a strategic asset, not merely a cultural constituency. The consulate said the forum was designed precisely to draw on the expertise of the Indian American technology community in the Greater Seattle area.

What to watch

The forum produced no announced deals or commitments — it was a deliberative gathering, not a summit with deliverables. Its value will be measured in what follows: whether the discussions on AI infrastructure, semiconductor design and quantum research translate into concrete collaborations, talent pipelines or investment flows between the Pacific Northwest and India.

With the India AI Impact Summit 2026 setting the policy frame, events like Ideas4India are where the follow-through gets negotiated. The consulate has not yet announced whether the forum will become a recurring fixture, but the attendance — more than 40 sitting CEOs and CTOs — gives it a base to build on.
image_caption: Satya Nadella. The Microsoft CEO addressed Indian American tech CEOs at Seattle's Ideas4India forum.
nri_angle: For the Indian American community, the forum signals a growing role for diaspora tech leaders as bridge-builders between the US innovation ecosystem and India's technology ambitions.
